passage: Jasleen, you are worried about your new monitor badge, so listen. I am Alka, your Bua, and I was class monitor at ten. The badge felt like a crown. I stood at the door with my chin up and wrote names on the board. My best friend talked in line, and I wrote her name, but I skipped the new boy's name when he did the same, because he looked so lost. That night I felt a knot. Next day I told the teacher, "I was not fair." She said that was hard to admit. After that, I wrote names honestly, and I also said hello to everyone at the gate.

qa.q: How old was Alka when she was class monitor?
What did Alka feel when she first got the badge?
qa.a: She felt proud and grand, like wearing a crown, and enjoyed being trusted.

qa.q: What could Jasleen learn from Alka's mistake about being a monitor?
qa.a: Jasleen can treat friends and newcomers the same way and remember the badge is a duty to be fair, not a chance to boss anyone.

qa.q: How might the new boy have seen Alka's skipping his name?
qa.a: He may have felt relieved for a moment but could also have noticed that the rule was not applied evenly, and he may have felt like an outsider.

grounding: An elder recalls the pride of being a monitor, being unfair once, and learning to be fair to friends and strangers alike.
